chunks.arabic_text: عَبْدُ اللَّهِ بْنِ حَمَّادٍ، أَبُو مُحَمَّدٍ، الْأَنْصَارِيُّ، نَزَلَ قُمُ. لَمْ يَرْوِ عَنْ أَحَدٍ مِنَ الْأَئِمَّةِ (عَلَيْهِمُ السَّلَامُ). وَحَدِيثُهُ يُعْرَفُ تُرًا وَيُنْكَرُ أُخْرَى، وَيُخْرَجُ شَاهِدًا.

translations.en: Abdullah ibn Hammad, Abu Muhammad, al-Ansari, settled in Qum. He did not narrate from any of the Imams (peace be upon them). His hadith is sometimes recognized and otherwise denied, and he is brought out as a witness.

en.summary: This entry from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn al-Ghada'iri’s *Kitab al-Du'afa* profiles Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari, a resident of Qum whose direct transmission from the Imams is absent, marking him as a secondary link in the chain. His status as a *mudallis* or intermediate narrator is reflected in the scholarly practice of accepting his reports as *shahid* (supporting evidence) rather than primary proof, illustrating the nuanced criteria of *al-jarh wa al-ta'dil* in Shia hadith sciences. This reflects the broader tradition of evaluating narrators based on their proximity to the Imams and the consistency of their transmissions.
en.seo_question: Who is Abdullah ibn Hammad al-Ansari and what is his status in Shia hadith sciences?

key_terms.الأئمة: The Imams (plural of Imam, referring to the Twelve Imams)
key_terms.يخرج شاهدا: Is brought out as a witness/supporting narrator
